technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt a per-user-story work breakdown that maps 1:1 to the eight user stories (U1–U8) for traceability.
Treat the increment as a Spring XD → Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring Cloud Stream migration effort, so estimates include code archaeology from XD where applicable (U2, U6).

Use Spring Boot 3.x / Spring Framework 6 idioms (Java 17+) for all new/refactored code (U5, U7), and rely on the existing s-c-d/s-c-s Spring Boot starters rather than reinventing configuration plumbing.

For CI (U3, U8), use a hosted CI service (Travis CI/CircleCI-style YAML pipeline) with a Maven build matrix, since that is the de-facto pattern in Spring Cloud repositories; no new CI server is provisioned.
For U1, implement a thin shell command/wrapper on top of the existing REST endpoints (no separate transport), keeping the shell client stateless.

For U4, use Spring Boot's loader layout (PropertiesLauncher / custom classloader extension) to surface externally required JARs (e.g., JDBC drivers) at runtime, rather than bundling them into the Boot fat jar.
For U6, the deliverable is an investigation report plus a small reference prototype, not a production-ready HDFS module — HDFS work itself is out of scope of this increment.
For U7, design the REST surface around a single StreamController resource with sub-resources for lifecycle ops (deploy, undeploy, list, etc.), reusing Spring MVC and existing service-layer beans.
assumptions: The developer is fully proficient in Spring Framework, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring Cloud Data Flow, and the existing s-c-d / s-c-s codebases — no ramp-up time is included.
Effort estimates cover design, implementation, unit tests, and basic integration tests per activity. Code review is folded into each activity and not estimated separately.
All eight user stories are implemented by a single developer (per the prompt) and are estimated as if worked on sequentially with minimal context-switching overhead.
The XD reference codebase is available and readable; understanding XD internals is part of the activity estimates (not a separate research activity).
No production hardening, performance tuning, full documentation set, or release-engineering work is included — only what each user story minimally needs to be 'done'.
Java 17 toolchain, Maven build, and the s-c-d / s-c-s module layout are already in place; build/CI environments are green-field for the CI stories (U3, U8) only.
External dependencies (Redis server, HDFS, PHD cluster) are not set up by the developer; they are assumed available or mocked for testing.
Hour estimates are in work-hours, not elapsed hours; working time is ~8 productive hours/day implicitly.
